verdict.rationale: Simular's own docs describe a REST API, a Python SDK and an MCP server that let developers drive Sai's autonomous computer from their own code. Concrete endpoints for streaming events, approving steps and listing machines are documented, which directly supports embedding device control in an application. Missing for 10: no published OpenAPI/Swagger spec (all candidate paths 404), no independent or hands-on corroboration of the SDK/API, and API control of a user's own device (vs. cloud Windows computers) is not clearly documented.

support.subject: As a developer, I can embed device control in my own application through a documented SDK or API

citations.quote: gives developers, their code and their coding agents the same autonomous computer through a REST API, a Python SDK and an MCP server.
Developers can drive Sai from their own code or coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) with the Sai API: send a task in plain language, and Sai completes it on a cloud Windows computer.
`GET /v1/agents/events` streams progress; `POST /v1/agents/approve` answers an approval request; `GET /v1/agents/machines` lists your computers.
